objects.description: Small convenience byte string class wrapping std::string, providing Qt-like QByteArray interface (construction from C strings, size/data accessors, and append helpers). Manages its own storage via an internal std::string.
Non-owning view of a byte sequence, storing a pointer and length. Can be constructed from QByteArray or raw char pointers. Does not manage lifetime of the pointed-to data.

functions.name: KCodecs::base64Encode
functions.signature: QByteArray KCodecs::base64Encode(QByteArrayView in, bool useCRLF = true);
functions.description: Encodes the input bytes in Base64 and returns the encoded data as a QByteArray. The useCRLF flag indicates whether the output may include CRLF line breaks; exact wrapping behavior is not specified in this header. Typical usage: pass a QByteArrayView referencing the data to encode; the function does not report errors via return value.
requirements: The QByteArrayView argument must reference valid, readable memory for its entire size during the call.
If QByteArrayView was constructed from a const char* (null-terminated overload), the source string must be properly null-terminated to compute the length safely.
No constraints on the content of the input; arbitrary binary data is allowed.
The useCRLF parameter is a boolean; true may produce CRLF-separated lines, false should produce an unbroken Base64 stream. Exact line length/wrapping policy is unknown from this header.
Function returns a QByteArray and does not indicate errors via status codes; any error behavior or exceptions are unknown.

data_types.description: Arbitrary byte sequence with no required encoding or structure. May contain any 8-bit values including NUL bytes; not necessarily valid text. Suitable for functions that accept raw bytes for processing such as hashing, compression, or Base64 encoding.
